correctness.rationale: Every projected codimension-one assignment has a unique full completion; hence each top simplex has a distinguished free facet and a simultaneous collapse produces an (n-2)-complex. The full join is (n-2)-connected, shared (n-2)-skeleton gives (n-3)-connectivity, and an exact Euler-characteristic identity yields the positive Betti rank; Hurewicz/Whitehead or the graph case prove the wedge. The full-to-boundary restriction fails surjectivity since it maps q^(n-1) array assignments into q^n boundary assignments. Eleven exact finite chain checks corroborate, not substitute for, this general proof.

value.rationale: A currently studied finite-étale inflation theorem relies on surjectivity for every nested open, which can be mistaken for face-stalk surjectivity. This natural all-parameter family has unique local codimension-one lifting yet fails globally and has an explicit nonzero lower homotopy group with ranks growing in n and q. This sharp structural obstruction is useful for checking attempts to weaken hypotheses in homotopy and sheaf applications, and is not an arbitrary small enumerated example.
